subject: OrbisHealth websocket stalls during demo — exec escalation
messages:
From: Maya Bennett <maya.bennett@orbishealth.com>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin@redwood.com>
Cc: OrbisHealth CTO <cto@orbishealth.com>
Date: Tue, 4 Aug 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Realtime demo: stalled responses during patient-portal demo

Hi Soojin,

Quick note from this morning's integration demo — we started a 10-user concurrent demo of the patient summary stream and after a sustained burst (approx 40s) the UI started showing long pauses. In a few sessions the WebSocket connection emitted partial chunks and then stopped sending data for ~45–90s before resuming. A couple of clients received an error and the demo aborted.

We captured the client console and attached a screenshot and logs. Our CTO is copied — this was a board-level demo for a pilot decision. We need an immediate explanation of:
- What in the stack could cause multi-second/ minute pauses in chunked transfer?
- Whether this is a client backpressure issue, proxy buffering, or runtime stall.
- Estimated mitigation time and recommended temporary workarounds so our pilot isn't at risk.

Please escalate to your SRE/team leader; we need a warroom if this can't be fixed within a couple hours.

Thanks,
Maya Bennett
Director, Integrations
OrbisHealth

Attachments: orbis_demo_logs_20260804.tar.gz, screenshot-stall-20260804.png

From: Soojin Lee <soojin@redwood.com>
To: Maya Bennett <maya.bennett@orbishealth.com>
Cc: OrbisHealth CTO <cto@orbishealth.com>, david_kim <david_kim@redwood.com>, rishi_malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>, grace_oconnor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 4 Aug 2026 09:28:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Realtime demo: stalled responses during patient-portal demo

Maya — thanks for the report and the attachments. Sorry you hit this during a demo, we know how sensitive pilot demos are. I'm elevating to SRE and the runtime owners (cc'd).

Immediate plan:
1) SRE (David/Rishi): collect edge + runtime traces and inspect proxy 504s and keepalive counters.
2) If stalls are caused by proxy buffer exhaustion or idle timeouts, we'll ask you to switch the demo to the non-streaming fallback endpoint (blocking poll) for the remainder of the pilot while we triage.
3) We'll open a warroom if we don't have a short root cause within 60–90 minutes.

Please confirm whether you can switch traffic to a fallback endpoint (URL provided below) and share any additional client-side logs. We will share an interim exec note for your CTO within 30 minutes.

Fallback endpoint (non-streaming): https://api.redwood.com/v1/patient-summary?mode=sync

Thanks — Soojin
Sr. Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

Attachment: tail-stream-handler.log

From: David Kim <david_kim@redwood.com>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin@redwood.com>, rishi_malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>, grace_oconnor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>
Cc: Maya Bennett <maya.bennett@orbishealth.com>, OrbisHealth CTO <cto@orbishealth.com>
Date: Tue, 4 Aug 2026 10:04:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Realtime demo: stalled responses during patient-portal demo

Quick triage notes (initial):
- I pulled the provided logs and the edge request traces. We see a spike in concurrent streaming sessions at 09:03:12Z followed by a rapid increase in proxy queue length. Around that spike the edge LB reported an elevated rate of 502/504 responses to the client, and the streaming runtime (StreamingHandler v2) logged repeated "kv-cache: stall_detected" warnings.
- Chunked transfer frames are arriving at the proxy but the proxy appears to throttle writes to downstream sockets; several downstream write calls returned EAGAIN and were retried. That aligns with buffered-writes hitting the proxy's high-water watermark and the socket keepalive timers expiring.
- No obvious OOM in the runtime; CPU was elevated on a small set of pods but not saturating.

Immediate mitigations we recommend:
A) (INF) Increase proxy write buffer limits and reduce proxy idle-send timeout to avoid long pauses (config change).
B) (Customer-facing temporary) Switch Orbis demo to the sync endpoint or an alternate region to reduce surface area for the pilot.
C) (Short term) Restart the affected proxy pool (will drop in-flight streaming but should clear buffered backpressure).

I'm starting a limited rollback of a recent proxy config that touched chunk coalescing to rule that out; will update in 20m. If this is a third-party proxy (Akiva) we should loop their support — CC'ing them now.

-David
SRE Lead, Redwood Inference

Attachments: link to logs: https://drive.redwood.com/shared/orbis-demo-20260804, Jira INF-4921

From: Soojin Lee <soojin@redwood.com>
To: OrbisHealth CTO <cto@orbishealth.com>, Maya Bennett <maya.bennett@orbishealth.com>, David Kim <david_kim@redwood.com>, rishi_malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>, grace_oconnor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>, Akiva Networks Support <support@akiva.io>
Date: Thu, 6 Aug 2026 16:47:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Realtime demo: stalled responses during patient-portal demo — update and next steps

Team — follow-up after the warroom and triage:

Summary (executive): the incident was caused by a recent proxy chunk coalescing configuration combined with a burst of concurrent streaming sessions from the Orbis demo. The coalescing logic delayed flushes under certain backpressure patterns which, when combined with the proxy write buffer watermark, produced multi-second stalls and ultimately a small number of timeouts. No user data was lost; messages were buffered and later delivered once the proxy cleared.

What we did:
- Rolled back chunk-coalescing change in proxy pool (completed 08:35 PT 2026-08-04).
- Increased proxy write buffer and reduced idle-send timeout (config rollback + tuning).
- Restarted 3 affected proxy instances to clear buffered-writes.
- Added server-side tracing around StreamingHandler v2 to detect "stall_detected" events earlier.

Customer-facing mitigation offered:
- We provided the fallback (sync) endpoint to continue the pilot immediately.
- Redwood is issuing a pilot-service credit equal to one week of service (billing team engaged).

Next steps / action items:
- INF-4921: complete RCA doc and postmortem by 2026-08-10 (owner: David Kim).
- Engineering: add a safe-config gate for chunk coalescing toggles (owner: Rishi).
- Product/Solutions: review default keepalive/ buffer thresholds for streaming customers (owner: Grace).

Warroom notes and logs: https://drive.redwood.com/shared/orbis-demo-20260804
Jira: https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/INF-4921

I will follow up with the formal RCA and the credit confirmation once billing finalizes. Apologies again for the impact during your demo; we appreciate the fast collaboration.

Best,
So Soojin Lee
Sr. Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
